abstract:
Online labor markets have become increasingly popular among companies seeking global access to workers. Some platforms have adopted a contest-based scheme, allowing employers to review multiple submissions before selecting the best one. This practice raises a crucial question: Given a predefined budget, should employers choose a contest or contract scheme for tasks? This study examines the comparative effectiveness of contests versus contracts in achieving better job outcomes, focusing on design tasks characterized by high uncertainty. Using a comprehensive data set from a leading online labor market, we employ multiple empirical strategies, combined with machine learning and text mining techniques, to examine the impact of compensation schemes on job quality. Our results suggest that contract-based jobs yield better performance than contests in the context of ideation tasks. Further analysis, such as examining image similarity among pairwise solutions within a task, identifies “copying” behaviors as a key mechanism undermining the effectiveness of contests. In the public setting of contests, workers can observe others’ submissions and revise their own, leading to imitation rather than innovation. As competition intensity increases, workers have weaker incentives to exert effort, reducing solution quality. Consequently, the negative incentive effects in contests outweigh both the potential positive incentive and parallel effects. Moreover, although information availability can enhance work quality, contests inherently offer limited informational advantages compared with contracts. Taken together, our findings suggest that contract-based schemes are more effective than contests for design tasks, offering important implications for both employers and platform designers in online labor markets.
                  This paper was accepted by Karan Girotra, operations management.

                  Supplemental Material: The online appendices and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.07082 .

ob.ai_reason: 在线劳动力市场研究，辅以机器学习
ob.tldr: 基于领先在线劳务平台的大样本数据，结合多种实证方法、机器学习与文本挖掘，比较固定预算下竞赛制与合同制对高不确定性创意任务质量的影响。结果表明合同制表现更优；公开竞争促使劳动者模仿并随竞争加剧降低努力，其负面激励超过竞赛的潜在收益。

title: Contest or Contract: Assessing the Effectiveness of Contests in Online Labor Markets
title_zh: 竞赛还是合同：评估在线劳动市场中竞赛的有效性
